questions.question: Which failures should trigger a retry?
questions.context_md: Right now `fetchJson` throws on a network error (fetch rejects) and on any non-OK status. Retrying a 4xx like 404 or 401 will almost never help.

options.label: Network errors, 5xx, 429 and 408 only; other 4xx fail at once
options.impact: Common practice; no wasted retries on client errors

options.label: Network errors and 5xx only
options.impact: Simpler; a rate limit (429) fails at once

options.label: Any failure, including all 4xx and JSON parse errors
options.impact: Simplest; wastes retries on permanent errors

questions.question: How long should it wait between attempts?

options.label: Exponential backoff with jitter (about 200ms, 400ms, 800ms), and Retry-After is honoured when present
options.impact: Spreads load out; adds a little complexity

options.label: Exponential backoff without jitter (200ms, 400ms, 800ms)
options.impact: Delays are predictable, so tests are simpler

questions.question: Should callers be able to configure retries?
questions.context_md: The signature is currently `fetchJson<T>(url)`. I found no callers in the repo.

options.label: Add an optional second argument `{ retries?, baseDelayMs? }` with the defaults above
options.impact: Signature stays backward compatible; tests can set the delay to 0

options.label: No options; the policy is hard-coded
options.impact: Smallest API; tests need fake timers

questions.question: What should be thrown when every attempt fails?

options.label: The last attempt's error, with the attempt count added to the message (e.g. `<url> answered 503 after 3 attempts`)
